title: An Input-Aware Sparse Tensor Compiler Empowered by Vectorized Acceleration
problem: Sparse tensor computations (especially sparse matrix-matrix multiplication) suffer from poor performance due to rigid sparse formats and limited compiler support for diverse sparsity patterns. Existing tensor compilers offer limited sparse optimizations, forcing practitioners to choose between manual kernel design (high effort) and generic code generation (suboptimal performance).
motivation: Sparsity is ubiquitous in real-world deep learning, graph algorithms, and scientific computing. Efficient sparse code generation on heterogeneous hardware requires input-aware format selection and vectorized kernel optimization, which current compilers do not support well.
method: SpMMTC looks at where the non-zeros are in your input matrices before compilation and generates optimized instruction sequences specifically designed for that sparsity pattern—this is faster than generic code because the custom version can skip zeros and efficiently use the CPU's parallel capabilities (SIMD, which executes multiple operations simultaneously). The compiler automatically adapts to what the hardware can actually do, checking the CPU's parallel width (SIMD width) and memory cache structure, so it generates fast code without requiring manual programming. It employs two key optimization techniques: vectorization guidance ensures the CPU's parallel hardware is used effectively, and pattern-aware loop unrolling (expanding loops to expose more parallelism) maximizes the opportunities for parallel execution.
key_novelty: A compiler that inspects each input matrix's non-zero pattern and automatically creates optimized code specialized for that pattern, without manual per-matrix tuning.
contributions: Input-aware compiler analysis of non-zero distribution in sparse matrices
Vectorized kernel generation targeting specific sparsity patterns and hardware ISA
Speedups of 1.21–2.97× over TACO, TVM, and ASpT on multi-core processors
1.52× speedup for sparse MobileNetV1 inference on edge devices

metrics.speedup: 1.21–2.97× vs. TACO/TVM/ASpT; 1.52× for sparse MobileNetV1 inference

limitations: Evaluation focuses on multi-core CPUs and edge devices; applicability to GPU/accelerator sparse operations not discussed.
primary_theme: Input-aware vectorized compilation for efficient sparse tensor operations
